key_insight: A message-passing reinforcement learning policy combines global network decisions with local node actions while respecting permutation symmetries and transparency constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports coordinated control of interconnected systems, including capital budgeting and institution-level interventions to manage financial systemic risk.
method: Use a message-passing neural network with separate global and local policy heads.
Derive explicit Lipschitz bounds for input and parameter perturbations.
Use these bounds to establish convergence guarantees for projected policy-gradient optimization.
evidence_signal: Financial-network experiments report better performance than feedforward-network baselines and scalability to large networks, but the abstract provides no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Robustness and convergence bounds depend on architectural choices and graph characteristics, so sensitivity should be checked for the target network.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
